evidence.text: Bank7 won the court auction for 71% of Century Financial on 2026-09-03 with a $91.0M bid ($88.96M net of a $2.04M break-up credit, up from the $68M stalking-horse price). It then signed a full merger agreement on 2026-09-16 ($70M cash + 1,232,657 BSVN shares, ~$137.3M). The Q2 call set the Q3 noninterest expense guide at $9.5-9.7M and said 'M&A transaction expenses are more difficult to estimate', i.e. outside the guide. Q3 GAAP EPS is therefore likely to carry auction, legal and advisory costs that a $1.00-1.08 consensus may not include. Each ~$1M pre-tax is ~$0.08 of EPS on ~9.6M diluted shares.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was a GAAP headline miss ($0.87 vs $1.03-1.04) driven by a one-off energy-asset loss and M&A/IT costs, with core EPS cited at ~$1.06. The stock moved -2.51% on the release (baseline) and has since drifted up ~8%, so holders looked through the one-off within weeks.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus for this two-to-three-analyst name has not visibly moved since the deal. Earnings Whispers still shows a $1.00 consensus and a $1.06 whisper, above the Q2 GAAP print. If merger costs were modelled in, the estimates would sit below the ~$1.05-1.10 core run-rate the guide implies. They do not.
evidence.independence: The Q2 call transcript gives the expense guide and its exclusion of M&A transaction costs (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). The 2026-09-17 merger 8-K and investor deck say deal metrics 'include transaction-related expenses' but give no amount (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036855/ef20081983_ex99-2.htm). evidence.text: On a core basis, the company's own Q3 guide implies EPS at or slightly above the bar. Core NIM is guided to 4.45-4.53% on ~$1.83B of earning assets, so ~$20.5-20.9M of core NII, plus loan fees from the 'significant paydowns' expected in H2. Q2 reported NIM was 4.81% including fees, and NII was $21.91M. Noninterest income is ~$1.0M with oil and gas revenue now gone (the properties were sold 2026-04-10). Expenses are guided at $9.5-9.7M against ~$9.9M in Q2 excluding the $2.0M of oil-and-gas expense. Provision has been zero for two quarters, on a $19.5M ACL. That arithmetic gives roughly $1.05-1.10 of core EPS against a $1.00-1.08 bar. The result sits inside what management guided.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Clean beats of +$0.09 to +$0.24 bought +0.57% (Q3 2025), +1.34% (Q4 2025), +1.89% (Q2 2025) and +2.4% (Q1 2026). Beats in Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 still fell 3.2% and 4.8% in weak tapes (baseline). The name beat 6 of its last 7 quarters (MarketBeat).

evidence.independence: The guide figures come from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) and the oil-and-gas exit from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746129/000114036126032024/bsvn-20260630.htm). The Q4 NIM and NII outlook given on this call should be firmer than the static baseline the market was handed in July.

evidence.text: The Century merger is on an accelerated path. Century shareholders approved it on 2026-10-09; Federal Reserve and New Mexico FID approvals or non-objections have been received; closing is expected about 2026-11-01, a month inside the 2026-11-30 termination date (8-K of 2026-10-09). The deal deck gives 25%+ EPS accretion, ~11% TBV dilution, a 1.7-year earnback, pro forma CET1 of 10.0% and TCE/TA of 8.3%, a $3.3B pro forma balance sheet, and a price of 6.3x 2027E earnings plus synergies. This call is the first earnings call since the merger agreement and will carry pro forma commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior earnings call has carried an acquisition this size (the deal ~doubles assets from $1.9B). The stock is +8.2% since 2026-07-16 through the auction win and merger announcement, so the deal has been bought, not sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The deal metrics are public and the stock is near its high. The 5-day run-up of -0.2% shows no reaction to the 2026-10-09 approval 8-K. The unpriced part is any confirmation or change of the accretion number, cost saves (the deck gives no dollar figure) and Century's actual earnings, which are not disclosed anywhere.
evidence.independence: The investor deck has the metrics (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036855/ef20081983_ex99-2.htm). It shares the company as the source. evidence.text: The balance sheet was flat to shrinking in H1. Gross loans went from $1,609.4M at 2025-12-31 to $1,600.1M at 2026-06-30, with agricultural loans -$16.9M and C&I -$24.1M. Deposits fell $63.0M to $1,637.8M. Yet the full-year guide is mid-single-digit loan growth, with 'significant paydowns' in H2 and Q3 fundings expected at roughly double Q2. Hitting the guide needs ~10% annualized H2 growth, so Q3 period-end loans are a visible test. Paydowns also lift loan-fee income, which offsets part of the hit.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed flat loans YTD alongside the headline miss: -2.51%. The line's separate effect is not isolated.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 10-Q loan table is barely read on a two-to-three-analyst name. If the market doubted the growth guide, estimates would have fallen after Q2. They did not.
evidence.independence: The guide language comes from the call transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/bank7-bsvn-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). Both are company documents, so this is one fact pattern, not two.
